utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome, to continue with your rebuttal case, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Ms. Friedman is going to take the next witness, and she has a preliminary matter she would like to raise with respect to that witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. The preliminary matter is to be dealt with in private session. Are we in private session right now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphones haven't been switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please switch on the microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you may sit and you may begin, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has granted you protective measures in the form of image distortion and the use of a pseudonym, so I will refer to you as VG-141. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And could the witness be shown her pseudonym sheet, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: My usual notice, if it's possible page 3, line 8 just to be redacted the name of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it has to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: On the piece of paper before you, can you confirm that this is your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And could you please sign this sheet of paper?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I tender the pseudonym sheet as an exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P324, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, before you is just a pseudonym reference sheet, it's an excerpt from the first one that shows a name of another woman and the pseudonym we used for her in court. Do you know this woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would ask that if you do refer to her in your testimony, can you please use the pseudonym you see before you, VG-136.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sorry, that's VG-133. Is that the number that you have before you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. VG-141, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And in what municipality were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Where were you living in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I was living in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: When did you meet Milan Lukic for the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I met him for the first time at the door to my flat on the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: What were you doing on that day before he arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I was in my flat with my mother, my brother, and my father. It was dusk, evening, 7.00. We were playing cards and dominoes because the situation was tense, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And who answered the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I opened the door.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And can you describe what the man before you looked like?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: He was about 25 years old. He was tall. He had light brown hair. He was about 1 metre 80 tall. He had one of those short rifles, I don't know whether it's a semi-automatic or whatever, but anyway a shorter rifle, but on his back it said "milicija" in Cyrillic, police.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: You said it was around 7 p.m., was it still light out around that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what about in your apartment, did you have lights on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: No, because it was June and still light, there was still daylight, we didn't have the electricity on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And how far away were you standing from the man that came to your door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, when he rang the bell, I opened the door, so I might have been a metre or less away from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: He said, Good evening, any men in the house? We are looking for Sehic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Did anyone else come to the door at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: My father came to the door and asked who he was looking for, and he said, Is Sehic there? Do you know Sehic?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: My father said he didn't know any such man and that there wasn't a Sehic living in the building, but there is a neighbour of ours and his surname was Sehic and that he lived on the fourth floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did anybody else from the house come to the the door?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Milan Lukic asked whether there were any other men in the flat. My brother came to the door so both of them were at the door and he said that they should follow him and show him where that other flat was, that is to say, where Sehic was.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Did they ask or inquire anything else of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: My father just asked whether he should take any ID papers with him or anything else, and he said no, just follow me, you don't need anything.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And where did they go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Milan Lukic -- well, in the meantime, he rang the neighbour's doorbell and our neighbour opened the door and her son was taken out of the flat together with my brother. And they set off down the stairs. We lived on the fifth floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where did they go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: They left the building. And my flat as I said was on the fifth floor as I looked out on to the street. My mother and I went out on to the balcony, and you could see the street from the balcony, and there was a red Passat car, a dark red Passat car parked in front of the building, and my brother, my father and my neighbour Mirsad was standing in front of the car when Mirsad Hota's [phoen] father appeared who was coming out of the garden; and he said, Leave my child alone, take me instead. And the gentleman said to him, You old man, you are coming with us too.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, you mentioned the dark red Passat. Do you have any other information about that car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, I know that it was owned by Behija Zukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: If it was being driven by other people that day, do you know now that came to pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, Behija Zukic was the first victim to fall, that is to say the first person killed in Visegrad. Visegrad is a small town, not a rich town either. And at that time, that was considered to be a luxury car, and there was only that one Passat car in Visegrad so everybody could recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did you hear how Behija Zukic was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, I heard that she was killed in her own house, and that they seized her car and that Milan Lukic took the car.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Did you see any other vehicles when you looked out from the balcony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I noticed a green Skoda, and I recognised Mitar Vasiljevic. He was in front of the building too.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: How did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, I knew him because he worked as a waiter in the hotel by the Drina river in the garden restaurant there and we would go there fairly often. The garden of the hotel.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: You said that you were observing this from your fifth floor balcony. Do you know if anyone else in the building had an opportunity to observe what was happening below?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: My mother was on the balcony with me, and my neighbour whose son had also been taken off, and, unfortunately, the woman has died since; and below us on the fourth floor, there was witness VG-133, her father-in-law and mother-in-law, they were also on their terrace. And they could see it all.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, were the men at any point put in one of the vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes. They went into the red Passat car.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And who was driving the red Passat car, if you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us what you observed at that point?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The car set off towards the bridge across the Drina river, and as my building is about 100 metres as a crow flies from the bridge, so not far, and as I live on the fifth floor, I could see the bridge from there and I saw this car stop on the -- at the middle of the bridge at a wider place that is called the divan [phoen], and I saw my father, my brother and neighbours climb up on to the divan; and it has two steps where the end of the bridge, the wall -- I could see my brother, my father, and my two neighbours that I've already mentioned. My brother was wearing a white jumper and a light grey track suit, and I saw that he put his hands up in protest. I couldn't hear him say anything, but he kept his hands in front and he was debating something, and I was wondering what was going to happen because I had heard that there were mass killings that took place on the bridge. So I turned my head, I just turned my head towards the wall, shut my eyes, covered my eyes with my hands and then I heard shots. I don't know how long this went on for. It seemed a long time to me, but it might have been just a few minutes, one or two minutes, and when I turned around again to look at the bridge, there was nobody there. My brother wasn't there, my neighbours weren't there, my father wasn't there anymore. All I saw was that somebody was leaning over the wall of the bridge and looking down into the water. Then I rushed into the flat, and there was a radio Visegrad broadcast and I listened to that and heard that all the citizens, locals who were being taken off, that that should be reported to the police. So I rang the police up and said that a uniformed individual took away my father and my brother, that they were up at the bridge, and could somebody check and see what had happened. And they said they would check this out, but I never received an answer from them. My mother and I were crying and all we could say is what has happened? What is this that has happened? And at that point in time, the Passat car was still on the bridge, but they were no longer there, that is to say my brother, my father, and my neighbours. They weren't on the bridge anymore.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you said that at the time you referred to him as a uniformed soldier, and when did you find out that this was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Perhaps half an hour later when we went down to our neighbour's flat. The father-in-law and mother-in-law, VG-133, said, the neighbour said that this was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I really apologise for interrupting, just one intervention in transcript, page 9 lines 13 and 14, I think the translation should be "to report to police." And we can listen the tape or my learned friend from OTP could clarify by examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Instead of what?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Locals who were police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: To report to police. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, so the father-in-law and mother-in-law of VG-133 told you it was Milan Lukic. What did they say about how did they know this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: They said that before he same came to our flat he had been to their flat and asked for their son, and they recognised him and it was Milan Lukic. Just like VG-133, she said it was him too, that is to say Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: So turning to each them, VG-133, did she tell you how she knew Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, she knew him because she had worked as a nurse and he would come to the the health centre, so she knew him. And on several occasions, he came to her flat looking for her husband.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: How much longer after the incident did you stay in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Seven days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And how did you come to leave Visegrad after my brother and father disappeared, they came on a couple of other occasions, that is to say soldiers came to check out the flats to see if there were any other menfolk in the flats. And on one occasion when they took some Muslim inhabitants out, I wasn't there at the time, I was in my flat actually, but as I had the keys to the building, because we would shut the down stairs front door, a soldier came by and returned the keys to the the entrance to the building, and I asked him how long we could stay there, and he said that convoys were being prepared and that we would have to leave the town, and that the convoys were safe; and our neighbour called my mother up on the phone and she was a Serb, but she was a very good neighbour of ours, and she told my mother that we should leave with the convoy and that she was, in fact, saving me. She gave us some money and even prepared some food for the journey and wished us bon voyage.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: What day did you leave on a convoy?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The convoy was planned on the 16th of June, but on that particular day there was some shooting around Sjemec, so the convoy was moved forward to the 17th. And that night we didn't stay in our flat, we didn't sleep in our flat, but together with our neighbours who were Muslims as well, who had remained in the building, we spent the night in Witness VG-133's flat and set out from in front of the Visegrad hotel, that is to say the hotel on the Drina, we set out with the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And where was the last stop of the convoy, where did it take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The convoy took us in the direction of Olovo, and we passed over Serb-control territory and along the separation line, 5 kilometres from Olovo, that's where the buses were stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: When you arrived in Olovo, how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: We stayed in Olovo for two or three days. My mother wasn't feeling well, so I took her to the health centre there, and then we were taken to Visoko by bus.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: How long did you stay in Visoko and where did you go afterwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: We stayed in Visoko for a month and a half, stayed with some of my father's relatives, and through the Red Cross, I met my aunt from Gorazde there and then we left for Germany.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. When you were in Germany, did you ever report this incident to the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: In Germany we had very good support from friends. I mean, they were Germans, and there was a professor and he was extremely kind to us, and I told him what had happened; and through the Red Cross he filled in the forms for the missing persons in order for them to look for my father.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, while we are wait for that, I can at this time perhaps voice my objection. This is, indeed, the document that I mentioned earlier. This is a statement of some type of various facts resulting from Ms. Ewa Tabeau and Arve Hetland. It is based upon communications with several organisation including Amor Masovic's group. So in essence, it a third party statement recording hearsay information of other third parties being presented, and to the extent that that does not come from this witness, I would object to this document coming in as a stand alone document of itself without the proper formalities being followed, i.e., calling Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The document is self-authenticating. It is the same information that the court has heard extensive testimony from Dr. Tabeau about, the first page of the document lists the source that were used. They were all sources that were used in her previous report and in the clarification, so in that sense the document should not have any problems in terms of authenticity; and I will ask the witness to confirm the contents of the document, which is the part that she can comment on; but it's well known by now in these proceedings where this information comes from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You say it is the same information in relation to which we have already heard testimony from Dr. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: It's the same sources that she uses to compile her report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Same sources.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: It's just a few pages very briefly about these two particular victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would say it's a violation of Rule 92 ter and 92 bis to present statements of persons whether or not they are accumulative of evidence that we still have certain formalities and procedures under Rules or Procedure and Evidence. And one of them is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down. Would the counsel please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They are not hearing you. You are going too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I apologise, Your Honour, trying to save time. I would say it's a violation of 92 ter and 92 bis, we still have formalities and formalities under the Rules of Procedure and Evidence at this Tribal such that even if evidence is cumulative of prior evidence those formalities must be met, especially where a written statement is being presented, being tendered by a party into evidence, purporting to have in it the statements of out-of-court declarants who themselves are relying upon hearsay of other persons known and unknown to compile the information and present it as for the truth of the matter asserted, which is, I think, what is being done in this case. It's very much similar to the report of Amor Masovic which this Trial Chamber struck in part where it contained un-confirmable statements of third parties that were not presented for cross-examination. And again the information here to the extent that it is something that this witness does not personally know or did not personally write would be out-of-court statements presented for the truth of the matter asserted and which would not be subjected to the scrutiny of cross-examination; and, therefore, we would believe would be violative of the Court's ruling as to the Amor Masovic testimony and also violative of Rules 92 ter and 92 bis, which are the proper modes of producing written testimony into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman, can you distinguish this from the Amor Masovic case.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I believe that there was -- I will have to check on this, but it was just one particular aspect of Amor Masovic's evidence that was not admitted; and I think it had, I think, it was specifically about the bodies having been moved from one site to another which was something that witnesses had reported to him. It was not about his use of the ICMP which is one of the sources that is a used here. It wasn't about his use of those demographic materials that were available. It was solely about something that he had heard from witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not the document is not from Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: It's from her colleague who works under her supervision, Dr. -- sorry, not doctor, but Arve Hetland, and he co-authored the previous clarification with Ms. Tabeau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Perhaps one final point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Also the version you have is signed by Mr. Hetland, but if it's necessary we can have an actual affidavit or declaration; and I would note that 92 bis does allow for such a thing for an appearance of such a witness not that I think this is a bis situation, but I don't see this document as being highly out of the ordinary for this Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber believe that this is a different situation from Masovic. We observe in the very last paragraph of the document that this witness actually provided the information that is in the in the document and she has already said as much. We'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Now, if I could ask the court usher to bring the document up on the screen. It's there. Okay. And turn, please -- if you could turn to the third page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, VG-141, you'll see -- does this document refer to your father and brother?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, should we perhaps not transmit this to the public.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I understand it's not being transmitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not being transmitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: VG-141, can you confirm that this relates to your father and brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And is this their correct birth dates?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, these are the correct dates.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And is this your address at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And could the court usher please turn to the fourth page now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, on this page the date of disappearance is listed next to the words "Visegrad." Can you read out that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The 16th of May, 1992. The 16th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us -- you had an occasion to see Mr. Masovic in Bosnia, can you tell us if you at that time said anything to him about these dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would object to the point that there's been no notice or disclosure of any discussions with Masovic including the proofing statement that was sent to us yesterday. There's no mention of any of this testimony. And the copy of the memoranda that was provided to Defence does not have the last paragraph that it say that it came from this witness, so I don't know what is going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I'm sure that the copy provided is the only copy we have, so it would have that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you find that for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to, Your Honour, the copy I have on the page two says, "The annexes to this memo list the personal details and details relevant to the reporting of death disappearance of," I won't say the names, "from the mentioned sources"; so it's clear that this does not come from the witness but from the sources that Ms. Tabeau's assistant identifies.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The paragraph that was referred to was the last paragraph on the first page. So that paragraph indeed reads biological -- some biographical data, that is the first name, family name, and date of birth were known of the victims from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: From the witness statement. There's no discussion here of the witness providing this information or speaking with Mr. Amor Masovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something. I did not see Amor Masovic. I was in his office, but one of the employees showed me the register of missing persons, and it is there that I found my brothers and my father's names. I did not meet Mr. Amor Masovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And in terms of the evidence we disclosed this exhibit as one we were going to use with the witness, so the Defence has notice of the exhibits of the witness's testimony, the fact that the date appears to be inaccurate and is the same everywhere else is something that I clearly should explore with the witness in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, the problem is that this witness did a proofing statement with this same counsel listed as corrections and clarifications of the statements by this witness. This information as to why the date is inaccurate is not on the proofing statement. They did not explain this difference in the proofing statement, and now they are attempting to do it as an ambush. And would he we knew that the date was different, we have a certain method of wanting to cross-examine that I think it's rather significant that the information provided by the witness to other organisations gives a different date of disappearance, and the only witness that this witness being brought is not for the event that is alleged, but the date. This is alibi rebuttal in the Prosecution's rebuttal case, the date is the critical part of this evidence and now they are changing the testimony, and they never gave us notice of it. That, Your Honour, is quite troubling.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, can you just very slowly and clearly outline your objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The notification for this witness, and in fact the submission of, one moment, the submission of 20 March, 2009, outlined the testimony that was going to be brought by this witness, again in rebuttal of the Defence case and in rebuttal of an alibi presented by Mr. Milan Lukic as to the 10th of June, 1992. The witness was proofed by the Office of the Prosecution on the 4th and 5th of April, 2009 and the proofing note was disclosed to us advising us of certain changes in the testimony and certain additional information from this witness, in the statements that were offered. This now explanation of this different date is not discussed in any of the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the date? What is the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: June 10th, 1992 and May 16th of 1992 because there is a report to the Red Cross states that the witness's father and brother disappeared on the 16 the of May, which of course would be of highly great interest to us because that means that the date that is for alibi rebuttal does not apply. This information that is now being elicited from the witness was not in the original documents provided to us, was not in the witness notification and is not in a proofing note; so I would like to know how it is that counsel knows about it, one, and is being permitted now to ask about it having not given notice of it to the Defence when it is a critical issue in this case for this witness and the reason that they are bringing this witness to establish that Milan Lukic was somewhere on the 10th of June, 1992; and it is the first time now that we are hearing this explanation of why the other documentation -- some of the other documentation shows that the witness's family members disappeared on a date other than the 10th of June. And I'm just troubled by the fact that it was not disclosed to us in any of the, I believe, it's four statements that were given to us, and the proofing note that was given to us, let alone the witness notification, so it's a matter of now I'm hearing for the first time this explanation, and now I don't know how to proceed with cross-examination on this topic. I was going to bring up the difference in dates and leave it at that but now I might want to do some more investigation. I do not know because I did not have notice of this change -- the material change in the testimony. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, this certainly not a material change in the testimony. As counsel has noted, there are four prior statements from this witness, one of which was taken by the the ICTY, three others taken in 2007. All four of these statements say that she saw her father and brother taken away and executed on June 10th. Now, what we did in proofing was we looked at these prior statements and the witness told me that there were a couple of minor points that she wanted to change so I provided a proofing note to that effect. Now, she is a viva voce witness so obviously her evidence is going to come when she testifies. I disclosed the exhibit. The discrepancy is apparent on its face. I'm entitled to ask about that and counsel is entitled to cross-examine on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed. We agree with the analysis put forward by the Prosecutor, Mr. Ivetic. You can cross-examine on the discrepancy.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I am just going to go back to see the last thing that the witness has said so that I ... Okay. So VG-141, you said that you had occasion to attend at an office in Bosnia where you saw this date of May 16th, and at that time you had a conversation about that date. Can you just say -- can you just tell the Chamber very briefly what your comment was at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I told them that the date was incorrect. And that day, the 16th of May, 1992, my brother and father were still alive and with us in the apartment. I told them that the date was incorrect. And I asked them how they came about this piece of information when they were still alive at that time. I told them that they were killed on the 10th of June, 1992. The employee in the office told me that all of the events in Visegrad -- well, as the reports were coming in they started drafting and putting their information together as of that date because it was as early as that that people were being taken away in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, Your Honour I have no way of cross-examining this employee of the office who was not here who is not here to testify; and I can't, therefore, cross-examine this witness on a critical point, a critical discrepancy in her evidence on the sole point that she's being brought here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, I would ask that we turn to page 5 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, actually, if we could redact that, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And can you on this -- can you please read out here the date of death. It's again located next to the words Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The 10th of June, 1992. Twice.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I tender this exhibit. I believe it was actually already admitted. Okay. So I tender it now, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P327 under seal, Your Honours and with your leave on page 4, line 7, the exhibit number should be P326, not P324. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Finally, VG-141, you've told us that this happened on the 10th of June, 1992. Can you tell us how you remember that it was precisely that date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: It was a difficult day for me. I will never forget it. I can even tell that you it was a Wednesday. I know that on the 11th of June, it was the day of Kurban Bajram. Since my religion is Islam, I observed that holiday. I am positive that it was the 10th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Does the fact that it was on Wednesday have any significance for you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: As a child, I used to say that Wednesdays are my happy days; but however, as of that day, Wednesdays are no longer my happy days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions for the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good morning, VG-141. My name is Dan Ivetic, and I will now pose some questions to you behalf of the Defence of Milan Lukic. Now, as much as our time is limited, I would ask to you pay close attention to what my questions are and limit your answers to those specific questions. Is that fair and understood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, first of all, I'd like to perhaps go into private session for the first couple of questions so as to protect the identity of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, VG-144 [sic] asked who the Milan Lukic that you say came to your apartment on June 10th, 1992, that was your first time seeing this individual; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And several times during your testimony, you identified Milan Lukic came to the door; it was Milan Lukic driving; it was Milan Lukic on the bridge. Prior to this date of June 10th, 1992, you did not know Milan Lukic personally, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I did not know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In fact in your sworn statement under oath to the ICTY Prosecution, you can see that at the time that this man came to your door and took away your family members, even at that time you did not know how this man was called; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I did not know what his name was.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the man that came to your door that day, help me out, he didn't introduce himself, did he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: No. Did he not introduce himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And your father and your brother, they didn't recognise him and say his name, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when that individual came to your door, if I'm correct, you answered the door; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I would imagine you only got a brief look at the man, that is to say, several moments?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I was at the door all that time when my brother and father appeared to talk to him, so it wasn't for as little as a few seconds, but I'd say several minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. And in those several minutes, you had occasion to view this man and to view his appearance. Then in your sworn statement so the ICTY Prosecutors at paragraph 4, you said the man was 1.8 metres tall, was about 26 to 28 years old with light brown hair. Do you affirm the sworn statement that you gave to the ICTY Prosecutor, the man you saw was aged between 26 years of age and 28 years of age?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: He appeared to be of that age. That's what I could gather.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you note any birth marks or facial hair on his face?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: No, I did not. He did not have a beard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How about any tattoos on his neck, arms, or any part of his body that was visible, did you see any tattoos?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I did not. I was looking at his face. I was not paying attention to whether he had any tattoos or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did he have -- what about the colour of his eyes, did he have blue eyes, brown eyes, black eyes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: At that moment I felt such fear that I could not pay attention to the colour of his eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's my point, you were quite scared at that time. A man you didn't know, and, indeed, you didn't know until later that someone told you this was Milan Lukic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I did not know Milan Lukic, that's correct, and I did not know it was he at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, am I correct that you were so scared and because of the circumstances when you saw this unknown person at your door, you would be hard-pressed to identify that person and name that person, that being your only encounter with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I remember what he looked like well irrespective of the fear I felt. I was fully aware of the person standing before me. I remember the face.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, the point is, ma'am, the person who told you that this was Milan Lukic, you cannot exclude the possibility that they are mistaken that this was Milan Lukic because, of course, you did not live that other person's life to know exactly what she thought Milan Lukic looked like; isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: No one told me what Milan Lukic looks like. I was only told that the person who took my brother and father away was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, ma'am, that individual who told you that that was Milan Lukic, you have no way of knowing whether that individual is mistaken or accurate, can you? You have no basis for that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The basis for my claim is that Milan Lukic seized Zukic, Behija's vehicle and that he could easily be recognised as the person driving that vehicle. It was that person that came in front of our building and got out of the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How would you have known that Milan Lukic seized Zukic, Behija's vehicle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me, I didn't understand your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm asking you because you told us that the basis for your claim is that Milan Lukic seized Zukic, Behija's vehicle, so I'm asking you what is the -- how did you acquire that information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Visegrad is a small town, you see. We heard what was going on, and I heard that many people had already been killed by Milan Lukic. I didn't know who Milan Lukic was, but when he turned up at our front door and when he took my brother and father away, and when my neighbours confirmed that that was who the man was because he had been to their flat beforehand, and so my neighbour told me and VG-133 said, Yes, Milan Lukic took away my father and brother together with my neighbour. And the vehicle was parked in front of the building so, well, the famous Passat car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's interesting, Witness, because in your statement that you've given here, never before did you identify that you knew it was Milan Lukic because of Behija Zukic's Passat. You never under oath either to the ICTY or to the Bosnian authorities never said that you knew that it was Milan Lukic because of the red Passat.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: That's actually incorrect. It's inaccurate. I can point to the statement where she says that this was the Passat that was taken from Behija Zukic. And I think she's being clear also today that that was just a final corroborating point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would submit differently, the witness testified she knew that Milan Lukic took this vehicle from Behija Zukic. That is nowhere in any of her statements. And I would ask counsel to show me where it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sure. It's in the statement of 2007 to the association -- the February 2007 statement at page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Read what is in that statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes, we will turn to that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Read the relevant part. In fact, just let it be placed. Read it for yourself, and let it be placed on ELMO. Do you have that statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honour, and I stand by what I just said. It does not indicate that she has knowledge that Milan Lukic took this vehicle from Behija Zukic. It identifies the vehicle and Behija Zukic's vehicle. In all of her statements this is the first time now she said she know it's Milan Lukic because he took Behija Zukic's vehicle. This is something that is not in her statement. The statement just says, I saw -- I should probably get the English version, it's easier.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Should we place it on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: It's then on the 10th page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My copy only has six pages. I believe it's the bottom of the second page.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Sorry, I was looking at the other statement where it also says --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I looked over the balcony and saw a red Passat car in front of the entrance. I believe that this car was the property of Behija Zukic from Dusce.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I would submit that's efficient. She's here to give her full evidence today, we don't know what question were asked during the interviews that led to these past questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Which is why I'm asking the question. I'm not the one who objected to the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I didn't object to the question. But I objected to the characterization that she has never mentioned this before. But also there is another statement that we can turn to, it's the March 2007 statement where she says, "Dark red Passat vehicle, which I knew was seized from Behija Zukic's family." In any event, further clarification is necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify that, madam. You said it was notorious and you knew at the time that this vehicle was taken by Milan Lukic. Yet in none of your statements did you link that to your identification of Milan Lukic; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was important for me to say Milan Lukic because I recognise him by the red Passat car.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, is it your -- is it an important bases of your conclusion that Milan Lukic took your loved ones away from your home on the 10th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, it's very important as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So now do you see why it is important for you to say whether, in fact, your knowledge of it being Milan Lukic is based upon that red vehicle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: It is well-founded. It was Milan Lukic. How many times do you want me to repeat that, and yes, he did drive Behija Zukic's red Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How many times do you see Milan Lukic driving the red Passat, and where is that in your statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I didn't see Milan Lukic until the day when he turned up at my front door, but I had heard that he drove the car and that he had seize the the car, confiscated the car after he had killed Behija Zukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There has been evidence led in this case, madam, that the red Passat was confiscated by the Visegrad police station. Would that knowledge change your conclusions and the definiteness of your conclusions that Milan Lukic was the individual that you saw on June 10th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are actually asking me. It was Milan Lukic. How many times do you want me to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness, but I am not the person who brought you here today to testify about a very important matter. You were brought here today to testify about the identity of the person that you saw on June 10th, I'm trying to explore how you know that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is badgering the witness. He is entitled to put whatever question he wants to, but he is not entitled to make this type of statement to a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I see nothing wrong with what I said, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: He is exploring the basis of her knowledge, which I think is he entitled to.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Mr. Groome, please. Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: He certainly is entitled to do that, to say I'm not the one who brought you here. This is all badgering the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, let me see if I can remember my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman and Mr. Groome, even with the misgivings that are associated with in-court identification, I have to observe that you haven't asked this witness whether she is able to identify the accused, whether the person who came to her door on that day, whether she sees that person in court. I know that you are relying on her statement that her neighbour told her, but I wonder whether in light of the practice that you have followed, consistently followed in relation to other witnesses, why you wouldn't have this witness attempt the in-court identification, as I said, even with the misgivings that may be associated with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly that question can be put to the witness and the Prosecution is willing to do that. Given that she only saw him for the first time and it was a rather limited opportunity, we thought that the jurisprudence of the Tribunal would clearly characterise her as a identification witness and wouldn't place much weight, if any weight on the in-court identification. Whereas other witness that we have asked that question to, and we haven't every witness to do that, but other witnesses we've asked that to, at least there was some basis for a Chamber fining that they were recognition witnesses, defined by the jurisprudence of the Tribunal and entitled to make such an observation but happy to put the question to her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I wouldn't require. It's a matter for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I would submit now that the Prosecution had their chance it would be improper for them to pose that question now seeing as how the witness has seen me consulting with my clients, therefore, has an independent basis apart from being able to identify him -- at to -- ID him in court now. They had their chance they didn't use it, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, I am I'd like to get back to this issue of how it is that you're so certain -- how you are so certain, not other people but you are so certain that was Milan Lukic. Am I correct that you heard a lot of bad things about Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Not a lot of bad things, just that he had killed a lot of people, and my conclusion is that those are bad things from personal experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So your entire knowledge of Milan Lukic is based on what other people say?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: This has been asked and answered, and also she has stated a knowledge based on that day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic, move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's talk about that knowledge. In paragraph 6 of your statement to the office Office of the Prosecution -- pardon me, paragraph 7, you talk about half an hour later going down stairs to your neighbour's apartment, I won't mention a name; but you specifically indicate there that when your neighbour told you it was Milan Lukic, "I did not know how he knew." Is that accurate, that you do not know how your neighbour knew it was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I didn't know how he knew at the time that it was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I return to the question that I asked previously, not knowing how your neighbour knew, not having been there when your neighbour met Milan Lukic or knowing the circumstances when they met Milan Lukic, would you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down. Would the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, the interpreters are asking you to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me begin again, madam. I return to the question I that asked previously, if you did not know how your neighbour knew it was Milan Lukic, if you had not lived your neighbour's life and been there when they say they met Milan Lukic or knowing the circumstances of how they met Milan Lukic, would you agree with me that you cannot exclude the possibility that your neighbour is mistaken and that individual that came on 10th of June, 1992, was someone other than Milan Lukic? Someone whose age is 26 to 28 years of age?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I do have to object that this was asked and answered because she has had that particular question put to her: How can you exclude the possibility given than you are not in your neighbour's mind. I think at this point it does border on badgering the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think he has a right to put it. Let's hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I gave my statements in Visoko, a picture was shown to me, a photograph, of Milan Lukic when he was younger, as he was when he came to the door of my flat. Now, if what my neighbour told me is not enough, that that man was Milan Lukic, on the picture, I was able to recognise that that was the same person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's interesting. How come you hadn't mentioned the picture earlier? And what statement is that in, because I have no information as to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution help me where that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no information of this either.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, you've been through a lot and this isn't getting any easier. It is not helpful to insert new material to try and bolster your identification.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's out of order. That's out of order.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm putting my case to the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, I'm not allowing that. I'm interested in the photograph. You must ask her about that and then she can be re-examined on it. The fact that she doesn't say so before doesn't mean it can't be raised here in court. It's for us to determine what weight to attach to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, and I've been asking her now 15 times, how does she know it's Milan Lukic? She mentioned the car, which she didn't mention before. She mentioned her neighbours [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... she has now mentioned a photograph, a picture. Let's hear about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When was this photograph shown to you, madam, and by whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: When I came to Visoko, after the convoy, I gave a statement there to that police there, the public security station in Visoko. I gave a statement there, and they asked me -- well, they asked me the same thing, how did I know that it was Milan Lukic, and they had some photographs there and on one of them was Milan Lukic. I pointed him out and they said, Yes, that's Milan Lukic; so that confirms it. All your questions, that my neighbour was quite right when he said that it was, indeed, Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention this to the Office of the Prosecutor, madam, if it was so strong evidence that it was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think there was any need to, to talk about a picture, when all my statements were based on the fact that it was Milan Lukic. Witness VG-133 told me the same thing, that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I want to focus on his picture?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. How many photographs were shown to you by the police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one. From that year, 1992, the way that Milan Lukic looked at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They showed you one photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you then identified that photograph as Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did they tell you that was Milan Lukic in the photograph when they showed it to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: They asked me whether I could recognise the man who came to the door, and they showed several photographs, and I recognised the person who came to my door and then they said that it was Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sorry I'm confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did they show you several photographs or one photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, several photographs. Several photographs of different people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I see. That wasn't clear to me by your earlier answer, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Nor to myself, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, this identification of the photograph, that's not included in any of the four statements that I have from you. Why did you not recount that -- you are very detailed in your statements as to how you believe it was Milan Lukic, you identify your neighbours telling you, you identify all that, yet you leave out this critical point of the photograph that you say was shown to you in Visoko. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, it was sufficient for me that my neighbours had confirmed that it was Mr. Milan Lukic, that that is who the man was. And I didn't need to talk about that photograph, but if you insist ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall what the individual was wearing in the photograph that you identified as being Milan Lukic in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: It was a camouflage, SMB, olive green uniform. He had no insignia, no cap on his head, just his hair. It wasn't black and white because it was a camouflage uniform, but he didn't have any insignia, any cap. His hair was a little disheveled, is that enough?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Was a written statement generated by the police in Visoko with respect to your photo identification of Mr. Milan Lukic as you've now testified to for the the first time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, your next question should have been: How were the other persons in the the photograph dressed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will defer to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Could you answer the Judge's question, how were the persons in the other photographs that were shown to you dressed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Well, they were all JNA. JNA uniforms of the SMB or olive green type.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Lukic's photograph was the only one in a camouflage uniform that you were shown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, VG-141, the issue of the May 16th date came up that was reported to the Red Cross as being the date when your loved ones disappeared and/or perished; and you told us in direct how that is, and unfortunately I cannot cross-examine the individuals in the offices that you claim you spoke with, but I would like to ask you this: Isn't it correct that your father and your brother were -- pardon me, your father was arrested and taken to the Visegrad police station on the 14th of May, 1992, where he was beaten and mistreated by Mr. Kojic and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. No, not Kojic. Kovac, Nebojsa.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. And I put it to you, ma'am, that the reason the International Red Cross date says the 16th of May, 1992 for the disappearance of your loved ones based upon information that you testified, you and your mother provided while in Germany through a professor, the reason is that they did not, in fact, return home from the police station in Visegrad after being arrested; isn't that the truth, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: My father returned on the 14th of May. He was taken away on the 13th and returned on the 14th of May, therefore, he was in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, I have no further questions four.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would tender the four statements into evidence so that they can be compared and contrasted. I have the ERN numbers for them, but it's my understanding that not all of them are in e-court. The Prosecution had disclosed some outside of e-court, so I am at the Court's mercy as to whether I should admit them as a group exhibit and perhaps get the corrected documents into e-court and then advise Madam Registrar accordingly once that is accomplished from my side, that would perhaps be the most efficient method rather to referring to documents that are not in e-court at present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D224, Your Honours. It will be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Under seal. Yes, and for the record, Your Honours, that will be the ICTY statement, dated 13th September 2008; the BiH statement, dated 27 March 2007; the SIPA statement, dated 18 April 2007; and the women victims of war association statement, dated 19 February 2007. Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Friedman.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: I have just a few matters for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Now, VG-141, with respect to the four different statements that you gave, can you tell us was it the same investigators and lawyers or different investigators and lawyers that interviewed you each time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Different ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And did they ask you the same questions each time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: They did.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Were there any different areas that you discussed in the different statements?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes. There were certain things that needed to be corrected. Mainly had to do with the medication that my father required, as well as regards the 10th of June, when the vehicle stopped in front of the building. One or two other cars arrived, although I don't know whether they came as a group of vehicles or the other two were just in passing. The Passat had already been parked. That was the difference in the statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I realise now that you are refer together I believe the sessions where you and I met and you told me about a few small discrepancies that you wished to correct; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. And I just actually was wanting to explore very briefly when you actually gave those statements in the past and there's been suggestion that you gave different information at different times; and I wanted to ask you whether the interviews were each exactly the same one like the other, or if they lasted different amounts of time and explored different subject areas?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: The differences were not great. It all had to do with the date when my brother and father went missing, or were taken away. It also had to do with who took them away. It all revolved around those issues.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Okay. Now, about the -- your father having been taken to the police station on the 13th and returned on the 14th. Is this information contained in your past statements as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And after your father returned on the 14th, was he -- did he go have occasion to go back into town, around town in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: He did not leave the house. When he was released from the police station, he was told that he was not to leave the town because there might be other interviews. Since then he spent all of his time in the apartment.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And because these statements are going -- have been entered, I think it's worthwhile to go through the two clarifications that the victim -- that the witness made, so that those are on the record as well because they won't be found in the statements. One is, as you you mentioned with respect to the cars and you confirmed that there were some cars that you knew were there and others you were not sure. Can you provide that evidence to the Chamber briefly about the three cars that you saw?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: In one statement you can find that there were three vehicles. What I can tell you now is that there were two. There was the green Skoda and the red Passat. I did mention a third vehicle, but I don't think it had to do anything with the the other two. These people may have just been passing by and stopped for a brief moment. That's all I wanted to say now.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: And there was one person that you mentioned not related to these incidents but related to the convoy, his first name was Goran, and you had a comment on that as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-141
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not certain of the name of the person who was escorting the bus on which I was when leaving Visegrad. In one statement, I stated that his name was Goran Krsmanovic [phoen], the other Goran Nedic. I'm not certain whether there was his correct last name. I do know that he worked at the police station. He was a policeman, since my father used to be a safety inspector as well. His nickname was Pedja, and he frequently visited us. I know what he looks like, but I'm not completely certain about his full name.

utterances.speaker: MS. FRIEDMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, I just wanted your corrections to be on the record and I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Friedman. Witness, that concludes your evidence. We are grateful to you for giving it, and you may now leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution now calls VG-136. Mr. Farr will be conducting the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit and Mr. Farr, you may commence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness 136, can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, the Chamber has ordered certain protective measures for you today and these are that we'll refer you to as VG-136 during the course of your testimony, and that the image of your face will be distorted so that you cannot be recognised. Therefore, please try not to mention any details such as your name or the names of members of your family by which you could you identified. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I understood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could I ask the usher to please provide the pseudonym sheet to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this sheet in front of you, can you confirm that the name and birth listed on that sheet are your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I would ask you to sign the sheet that the pseudonym sheet be then shown to Defence counsel and to the Chamber, and I would tender it as a Prosecution exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P328, under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, what is your nationality and religion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak of Muslim religion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Without mentioning the specific village, can you please tell the Chamber by municipality you lived in at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: In early 1992, I lived in the municipality of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you still live in Visegrad municipality today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you remember the date that you permanently left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I'll never forget that date. It was the 14th of June, 1992. The day and what happened on that day changed my whole life, and I will remember it to the day I die.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where you were on the morning of 14 June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: On the 14th of June, 1992, pursuant to orders from Vojvoda Ljubomir Ljupko Tasic of the village of Smirjece, Zagre, Velatovo, Gornji, Donji Dubovik, the inhabitants had to leave pursuant to his orders. And I was by the main road with the inhabitants of my village, with my family, following orders, we had to go down to that main road and to wait for buses organised by Ljupko Tasic to drive us in a convoy to Olovo Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: On the morning of 14th June, 1992, where were you when you first woke up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I was in the village. Dubovik.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And you've just said, I believe, that at some point in that morning you left your village, you left that village; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: We left the village and went down to the main road, and that part belonged to Dubovik, and it was called Mangalin Han, which was where the bus-stop was for the local bus routes and intercity bus routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What did you find when you got down to the bus-stop at Mangalin Han?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Going down the bus station and the road took us through the forest, we were followed by Serb soldiers and down at the bus station, we found a lot of other Serb soldiers there who were all neighbours from Veletovo, Bosanska Jagodina, and among them I recognised Ljupko Tasic, Dusko Maric, Dusan Simic, Zoran Gacic and his brother, Zoran and Pero Gacic too. And some other soldiers who were there whose names I can't remember just now and I might not have even known their names.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. And what happened after you arrived at the bus station and found these soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: We didn't wait long. The first bus turned up from the direction of Bosanska Jagodina, so I and my family got into the bus. I don't know if everybody could fit because there were people in there already from the Zagre, Smirjece, Velatovo villages up there, and anyway, we got into the bus and our bus set off for Visegrad, in the direction of Visegrad. And we arrived in Visegrad in the square in front of the hotel which was called hotel Visegrad at the time which was right near the old bridge that we call "tuprija" [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you please tell me the ethnicity of other passengers in your bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: In my bus most of the people there were Muslims, Bosniaks, and there were one or two Serb soldiers as well. In my particular bus, there was someone that came, that boarded the bus at Mangalin Han, but I see who that was and he was like an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you recall the names of any of the people who were in the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I do. In my bus were the following: Ferid Spahic, Esad Kustura, Musan Celik, Smail Zukic, and his family. There was my husband and Hasim Delibasic and his mother, his wife, and three minor children; they were under the age of five, all three of them. Then there was Fatah Kasapovic [phoen], Cena Kasapovic [phoen], Mina Kasapovic [phoen] and her child; there was the Hodja, the famous Hodja; Ibrahim Ibisevic [phoen] and his wife; Ahmedspahic, Amir [phoen] and so on; Hamed Ahmedspahic [phoen] and Abid [phoen] they were two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The transcript hasn't picked up all of the names did you just say that Ferid Spahic and Esad Kustura were the among the people on the bus with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, yes, they were. Ferid Spahic and Esad Kustura among all the others, yes, they were among all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened after the buses arrived at the main square? Excuse me, approximately what time did you buses arrive in the main square in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Between 7.00 and 8.00 in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what did you see when you arrived in the main square in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: When we arrived it at the main square in Visegrad there were lots of Serb soldiers in various uniforms there was the SMB olive green type uniforms camouflage ones with red berets on their head some of them. There was a lot of Muslim population by the department school called Visegrad Junke [phoen]. Well, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And how many vehicles did you see in the main square of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: As soon as I arrived, I don't know how many of there were in the convoy from Bosanska Jagodina to Visegrad, I don't know how many buses because I got into the first one so I don't know how many buses actually arrived from that direction, but as there were a lot of Muslim people there from the villages surrounding Visegrad, they brought in more buses from the bus-stop so in the square there were eight buses and four trucks. And all of those buses were full of people, full of the people from the surrounding villages in Visegrad municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. And what happened while you were on the main square of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
