utterances.text: Soon after we arrived there and when the buses were filled and the trucks too, a Serb soldier entered all the buses including my own and ordered that lists be made of all the passengers from my bus and from the other buses. I don't know who was in charge of doing this in the other buses, but anyway, in our bus, in my bus, Zulkic, Smajla [phoen] was the woman -- or rather was the man who was in charge of listing all the passengers, their first name, last names and date of birth. And when they made this list, when he made this list, a soldier came up and took the list away to the Vilina Vlas Hotel and that's what happened in the other busses too, with the other list.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: When the soldier came, he said to us that we could decide whether we wanted to go to Kladovo, Olovo, or Skopje, Macedonia; and as there were people in the buses who had family in Skopje, we decided to go to Skopje, our bus did, but they told us that we would nonetheless be going to Olovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And after that what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: While we were waiting for the column to be formed and for all of us to set out, my bus -- well, Milan Lukic came into my bus, boarded my bus, and he said, Is Esad Kustura here? And he was, I said Kustura was there, in the back of the bus; so he said, Yes I am, I'm here. And he said, Well, where are you my school friend? Just come out and go to the SUP for five minutes to give a statement. I didn't know Milan Lukic up until then and I would -- would that I had never met him even then; and there were people from his area, Zupa, from where he hailed and men there too that were younger than him that knew him, and I head them shouting Milan Lukic, Milan Lukic; and we held Esad by the legs to prevent him from going out. But he made his way through the bus who was -- which was packed jam. There must have been about 70 passengers in my particular bus. Anyway, he made his way through this crowd and just before he reached Milan, he took hold of the handles of the bus and swung himself, he had on a blue shirt and a bandage on his left hand. I could see that very well because I was sitting in the third row seat of the bus, and he needed one step to reach --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Just I am sorry for interrupting you. But you said, "... he took hold of the handles of the bus and swung himself, he had on a blue shirt and a bandage on his left hand." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I'm referring to Milan Lukic. Milan Lukic is who I mean. He was wearing a navy blue trousers and when Esad needed just one step to reach him, Ljubomir Tasic stepped on to the bus, Ljupko, his nickname is Ljupko, and said, What are you doing there? Meaning Milan and he just pulled him out, literally pulled him out of the bus and they went off some five or six metres were joined by Risto Perisic, and judging by the movements that Ljupko made with his hands he was hysterical, he was opening and shutting his mouth, well, I saw that he was actually probably swearing at him for upsetting his plan with respect it to the organisation of the convoy. And Risto Perisic, he was saying something too. I couldn't hear what he was saying because I was in the bus after all and this was some five or six metres away. And this exchange lasted for about five or six minutes and from somewhere Dragan Tomic came up to them and the four of them left and went to the Vilina Vlas Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. You've said that you did not know Milan Lukic before this day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I did not. No, that is correct. Perhaps I bumped into him in town sometime, but I didn't know who he was or that it was him. Anyway, he was tall --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've also testified that as soon as he got on the bus, other passengers started saying it's Milan Lukic, it's Milan Lukic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you remember specifically the names of any of those people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Ferid Spahic said it, Musan Celik said it, some women and young girls, some young girls who knew him said it, probably through their schooling or whatever. And Esad Kustura, he knew him personally, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You mentioned that Esad Kustura referred to Milan Lukic as his school mate. Do you know whether they, in fact, went to school together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I don't know. They are a younger generation than me. But probably they went to secondary school together, that's probable, because it couldn't have been primary school. Milan Lukic was from the Prelovo local commune, whereas Esad Kustura belonged to Visegrad, or rather his village did. So probably it was in second school that they were together.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know approximating what year Esad Kustura was born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Esad Kustura might have been born in 1968, 69, thereabouts. Either 1968 or 1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. This person who was identified to you as Milan Lukic, can you please describe him in terms of his height, his build, hair colour, eye colour, if you remember those things?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: He was tall, between 1 metre 70 and 80. Perhaps even taller than 1 metre 80. He had dark hair, sort of black. He was neither thin nor fat, of medium build. I think his eyes were black too.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I think that --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Or dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I think you've already mentioned some of this, but can you please describe how he was dressed on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: He was wearing light blue shirt with his sleeves turned up, and dark blue trousers, navy blue trousers, and he had a belt on his trousers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Was he armed as far as you could see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I didn't see anything. He might have had a pistol at the back somewhere, but I didn't see any weapon.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Was he wearing anything on his head?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: No, no. His hair was cut short and he was bare headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you see any insignia on his shirt or any other article of clothing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: No, I didn't, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You've said that after he got off the bus, Milan Lukic had a conversation with Ljupko Tasic and Risto Perisic. Approximately how long did that conversation last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Not long. Perhaps five or six minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And after that conversation, what did those men do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: They went off together to the Vilina Vlas Hotel, and the hotel was where the White Eagles, Beli Orlovi were put up.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Where was that hotel that you've just identified located?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Right near the square.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The hotel that you've identified as the Vilina Vlas Hotel, you are referring to a hotel that's --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Sorry, not Vilina Vlas, I meant Visegrad hotel. I made a mistake there. Visegrad hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, the hotel right next to the main square; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How far away were you from this person that was identified to you as Milan Lukic when you were -- when he got on to your bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a metre and a half, not further than that because I was sitting in the third seat. One and a half to 2 metres. I don't know what the distance is between the seats, the rows.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What were the lighting conditions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Good. The light was good.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: How long did the buses and trucks that you've referred to remain on the main square of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I think the column, the convoy left between 10 and 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you describe the formation of the convoy as it left the main square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: At the head of the column, there was a police car, and there was a flag of the International Red Cross put up. And behind that there was a 2-tonne TAM truck, I don't know what firm it belonged to. Then came the buses and the trucks were at the end of the column, so they took us off in the correction of Olovo and the Red Cross flag as they had planned to do and decided to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What was the first place the convoy went to after leaving the main square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: My bus went to the bus-stop to tank up with fuel, and upon returning from the bus-stop we joined up with the column again, the convoy again. The first place we stopped at was Garca or Mezalin, but I call it Mezalin right up to the new bridge. I call all that area Mezalin. Anyway, my bus stopped before the bridge. My driver was from the Centrotrans company, I don't know his name, but he had a moustache and his hair was thinning, and Radomir Limic, nicknamed Burdus another Centrotrans driver came into the bus, boarded the bus. He had a "sajkaca," a Serbian-style cap on his head, and there was a cockade on it, on the forehead, and he was armed with an automatic rifle that is called a dobosar, which is an old type of rifle. And he was wearing an SMB type uniform shirt and trousers. When he boarded the bus, he turned towards us and looked at us like this, and I noticed that his shirt and his trousers, his clothing was bloody. He sat down and he placed that automatic rifle on the seat. He sat down and as soon as we set off he started abusing us and he had lisp point when he spoke even he said, See how we are driving you, Alija wouldn't drive our Serbs, so we crossed the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. And sorry to interrupt, and after you crossed the bridge, where did the convoy go next?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: We went off in the direction of Lijeska.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And did you notice anything unusual en route to Lijeska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: The whole way from the institute for retarded children, there were Serb soldiers along the road, all the way along the route. They wore different uniforms, both camouflage and the SMB type; and as we were passing through the forest and it's a bendy road, anyway, I happened to see in a pit beside the road a woman, a Muslim whom who had been killed. I know she was Muslim because she had pantaloons, the type of pantaloons that Muslim women wore. They were multicoloured blue and white and her head was swollen like this and not far from her, I saw a thin man, he was dead too and he was -- he fell down in a sort of, he was crawling along, so he fell down in that position. He had brown pullover on and a shirt. And not from far from the man, I saw a horse that had been killed that was lying dead by the road and by a sharp bend, I saw a terrible thing and I'm sure there are witnesses who saw that too. I saw I came upon a terrible image, two Serb soldiers, one of them was kneeling or squatting and was roasting a man whose clothing had already been burnt off. The other one was standing there and drinking something from a beer bottle, glass beer bottle, probably alcohol. It was a terrible site to behold. And after that we reached Lijeska, which is where the busses stopped. I don't know it was whether Donja or Gornja Lijeska because I had never been there before and then the people who were escorting us --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you, witness, I just wanted to ask you what happened when you arrived in Lijeska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: The escort Nenad Pecikoza a colleague from work of mine got off the bus to get some sandwiches, he went into a small building, I don't know it might have been a school, it was on my right-hand side or some other side. Anyway, he went in there to fetch some sandwiches for the driver, and that's what the others from the other buses did. They went to collect the sandwiches, and we didn't stay there long, just 10 to 15 minutes, 20 at the most. I'm not quite sure how long, but anyway, we didn't have time to well, we didn't look at the time or take care -- but we took over the sandwiches. Or rather he took over the sandwiches.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Try to give short answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, witness. As His Honour as just mentioned, our time here is very limited so what I would like to ask you now is just what was the final destination of the convoy on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: The final destination was Isevic Brdo or Isevic hill, which was a place that did not belong to Olovo or Sokolac municipality either. That's what it was called, Isevic Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what happened when the convoy arrived in Isevic Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: When the convoy arrived in Isevic Brdo, Zeljko Tasic boarded my bus. He was an active duty policeman from the station in Visegrad and he had on his head a black "sajkaca" or Serbian hat; and he said that all men from 16 to 65 should remain the bus, whereas the women, children and people who were over that age should get off the bus, and that was what was done in other buses too. But it was Zeljko who came into my bus and told us that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you tell me how you know this person, Zeljko Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I knew Zeljko Tasic from my childhood because he was a neighbour of mine and he was an active duty policeman as well, so that as I say, Visegrad is a small town. There weren't many policeman and I knew them through life, through family connections, and so on and so forth. So I've known him since childhood. Early childhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are you aware of any convoys that left Visegrad in the days that followed the day that you left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes. Two more convoys came from Visegrad. I don't remember the exact date, but they followed us. We were in a village called Kolakovic for two days and then we were transported to Olovo and during that period two convoys arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you even estimate what the dates of those convoys were, if you are able?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Well, it's like this, we arrived on the 14th. We were up there for two days, so it might have been the 17th. Between the 17th and 21st is when both arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. I have a map here which is Prosecution 65 ter number 176. It is in e-court, but I'd like to work with it in hard copy because there's a lot of detail and I think it would be easier for everyone to see. Could I ask the usher to please provide copies to Defence counsel and the Bench and then place one copy on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, please take a moment to familiarise yourself with this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And if we could start by displaying the right-hand side, sort of from the right-hand border. Yeah, that's good. Great.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, are you familiar with the area depicted on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Does it depict some of the locations we've talked about today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I can point those out to you. This is where Bosanska Jagodina is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sorry, since our time is so limited, I would just ask you to wait for my questions. You mentioned that you were in the village of Dubovik on the morning of 14th June 1992. Do you see Dubovik on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, could I ask you to please place the letter D on the map beside the word Dubovik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. And could you circle that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. You've also mentioned events that happened in Visegrad town. Can you find Visegrad town on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Here it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could you please place the letter V beside Visegrad town and circle that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And finally you mentioned a location named Lijeska. Can you find Lijeska on this map and if you can please place an L beside it and circle the L.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Now, witness, after looking at this map --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: There is Gornja and Donja.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, so I see that you've made two Ls on the map in the location of Lijeska. After looking at this map, can you identify the road that the convoy you were on travelled from Visegrad town to Lijeska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Here.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can I ask you to please trace -- to please trace with the pen the a line along the road that you followed on that day from Visegrad town to Lijeska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Should I follow the road?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If the convoy followed the road, then please follow the road. Please show the route of the convoy.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally I would just ask you to write your pseudonym VG-136 at the bottom of the map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: One further question, earlier in your testimony you mentioned that along one of the roads you were travelling there were Serb soldiers standing along the sides of the road. Is that the same road or a different road than the road you've just indicated on this map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender the map as marked by this witness as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I have no more questions in direct examination.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P329, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, for 10 minutes, and then we'll take the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, my name is Dan Ivetic. It's now my turn to pose some questions. I'd like to start this area that you've talked to towards the end of your testimony. You described you went on the bus that you took a route, the route you've just described and along that route you saw two Serb soldiers sitting and the way I understood you said they were roasting a man either alive or dead. And you indicated that other people on the bus could confirm that which you said, and the first question I have for you, ma'am, is that other persons who claim to have been on a bus of the type that you allege, have, in fact, not mentioned this horrific sight of a man being roasted on a spit alongside the road. How do you account for that, ma'am, that you are the only one that recalls seeing that?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think she should be required to account for the testimony of other witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Quite so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it goes to credibility of this witness. She said that other people can verify what she said, and other people have not verified what she said. So I want to know what her explanation for that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But she can't account for the fact they that they didn't give evidence of that event.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask the question this way then.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, knowing that now other persons have come to testify under oath and no one has mentioned this horrific sight that you have testified to, does that refresh your recollection as to whether, in fact, you actually saw that or that you could be mistaken and perhaps made it up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I saw that for certain. Others may have seen things I had not. I'm not God to be able to see everything and certainly not a clairvoyant. Therefore, I couldn't see some things others did. However, it is impossible that I was the only person who saw this scene. Someone else must have as well. I'm not claiming everyone did, but it is highly unlikely that no one save for myself saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you -- actually to ask this question I would need to go into closed session, Your Honours, for the protection of a third party, not this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, today you said that you did not know it was Milan Lukic who came on the bus at the time that the individual came on the bus, and you said that some of your fellow passengers on that bus told you that it was Milan Lukic. And you indicated that Ferid Spahic and these others told you that it was Milan Lukic. Do you stand by that assertion that Ferid Spahic was one of the people that told you it was Milan Lukic on that bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I do. I do. Ferid Spahic stood next to my seat on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: He stood next to you. How close to you was he that he stood next to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Right next to my seat. He was holding on to my seat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the minute this individual came on the bus, he immediately told you or whispered that it was Milan Lukic that entered the bus, is that what you are telling us?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'm not sure she said immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking. Is that what she's telling us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: It wasn't only Ferid that whispered that to me, basically everyone on the bus who knew him said, it's Milan Lukic, it's Milan Lukic, but when they said that whispering --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I understand that. But with respect to Ferid Spahic is it your testimony that Ferid Spahic immediately whispered and said it was Milan Lukic when the individual came on the bus. Let's talk about him first, we'll talk about the others later.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, he did. As soon as he got on the bus, the people started whispering.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know that Mr. Ferid Spahic testified in these proceedings as a protected witness, and that's why we are in private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, ma'am, at page 530 of the transcript, lines 4 through 14 of the transcript, under oath, and under penalty of perjury, Ferid Spahic indicated that when, in fact, the individual came on to the bus, he did not know it was Milan Lukic, and he learned that at some later time. Now, knowing that Mr. Spahic testified the way he did under oath, do you wish to change your testimony which is also under oath and under penalty of perjury?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I don't want to change my opinion or my statement. He did say that behind my back standing there. As for his testimony, I don't know what he testified to.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is it your testimony here today that Mr. Ferid Spahic lied to this Court under oath?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's certainly something that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: She never said that, let's move on, we have heard it and it will be for us to determine how to deal with the apparent inconsistency.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Discrepancy. Your Honour, do we still have time? Or is it -- I forget when the 10 minutes started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go to quarter past.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If we could go back into open session then.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam, I'd like to talk with you a little bit about this individual that came on the bus that you say is Milan Lukic that you never knew before the date in question, et cetera. Am I correct, looking at your proofing notes, that is to say the corrections that you made with the Office of the Prosecutor, that the Milan Lukic that you claim got on the bus had sleeves of his shirt rolled up such that you could see his bare arms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, other Prosecution witnesses that have testified before this Tribunal, have mentioned some sort of double eagle tattoo on the arms of the Milan Lukic that they identified. Do you recall seeing such a tattoo on this individual who you claim is Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I did not see it. I can't tell you I did when I didn't. I only saw the bandage, and it was because the bus was swaying while going through the curves. I saw no tattoos.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, did this individual who got on to the bus that you claim as Milan Lukic, did he announce or introduce himself, or is your testimony as to his identity related, based solely upon the whisperings of other passengers on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes. People were whispering. I didn't know him. Had I known him, I would have recognised him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me clarify. So is the sole bases of your identification of Milan Lukic the whispering of other people on the bus?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to these people that were whispering, you have no way of knowing whether they were mistaken or accurate as to this being Milan Lukic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: How could they be wrong if they knew him? They can't say it was me when they knew it was him. They had to say it was that person. They could not have picked just any name. They must have known him. Had I known him, I would have been aware that it was he who was on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you are speculating that because they used his name, they must know him; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I'm not speculating. It was the people who kept saying Milan Lukic, Milan Lukic; and they tried to make him stay on the bus. I guess some of them knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, do you know that there's been evidence led in this trial that Milan Lukic left Visegrad sometime during his third or fourth year of high school and did not return to Visegrad for several years. Does that effect your speculation as to whether persons knew him or could perhaps be mistaken? How can you be so sure?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Many people left after the fourth or fifth grade and then returned to Bosnia in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, we'll take the break and please remember the time-limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a brief matter before we -- I'm going to ask the Chamber to consider something over the break. I've just received an e-mail from the interpreter who has been sitting with VG-022, the next witness. He is a protected witness who is coming back to testify briefly about two matters. He has asked the interpret to convey to me, which I now convey to the Court, he is asking whether it's possible for his voice to be distorted. The last time he testified he says that everyone knew who he was by his voice, so he is asking would the Chamber consider allowing him to have his voice distorted for his testimony on that occasion. I'll ask for the Chamber to consider that over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we will.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One addition to that then if you are going to consider that. If he has already testified as VG-022, they know who he is, this whole discussion is revealing who he is and he should be under a different pseudonym.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'll consider that, Your Honour, I'll discuss that whether it's necessary -- I'm just afraid of the confusion it may cause changing pseudonyms midstream.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour, it looked like you were about so say something, I was waiting for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, I'd like to finish up a few more questions with the time in the bus in the individual which you claim was Milan Lukic came on board before moving on to some other topics. Now, from your testimony as to Mr. Esad Kustura, I believe you said you had to travel through the crowd, and there were about 70 passengers on the bus. I got the impression that Mr. Kustura was sitting at the back of the bus; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes. He wasn't seated, but he was standing in the rear of the bus behind me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, you have 20 minutes and we have to apply the time strictly. I want the parties to bear that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I appreciate that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: With respect to where he was standing at the back end of the bus, approximately how far was that from where you and the other individual we mentioned in closed session were standing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Perhaps 2 metres behind me or even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if I can ask you, you indicated that persons were tugging at his legs trying to keep him from advancing towards the front end of the bus. Who were these persons, and how many, and where were they seated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: We all did. Even I was trying to stop him since he is a cousin of mine. I tried to tug at his pants to stop him. He held a leather jacket in his hand. Everyone was trying to stop him, although I cannot tell you everyone by their names but basically everyone was trying to prevent him from getting off the bus, mainly women, and girls who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me try to understand something, you said even I tried to tug at his pants to stop him. Why would you do that if your testimony was that you didn't know who this person was that came on the bus, you didn't know whether that person was there to help, Mr. Kustura, you didn't know any of that why would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's not completely accurate as to what her testimony is. Her testimony is that she believed the person was Milan Lukic based on what all the other people on the bus had told her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let me ask you it this way at the time that you tugged at Mr. Kustura's pant leg, did you know it was Mr. Milan Lukic who was calling him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I heard it from the people who said it was Milan Lukic. According to their words, I knew it was Milan Lukic. They must have known him since they were saying it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My point is, why were you tugging at his pant sleeve? If it was a friend of his calling him, you had no idea to know this individual was not going to help them. Why did you make the decision to tug at this gentleman's pant leg?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: You know what, I heard a lot of ugly things about Milan Lukic and the things he had done. There were people who went through some things because of him, and it is for that reason that I believed he would do harm to this man. I was not an observer, witness or participant in any of his acts. I did not see those things. I only heard it from other people, and that's why I was afraid that he would hurt this person as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Since you did not know Milan Lukic before he stepped on the bus, how long did it take for these people to tell you that it was Milan Lukic to tell about all these horrible things that Milan Lukic had said and done? How long did it take for these people to tell you these bad things about Milan Lukic while Mr. Kustura was walking up to the bus?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think that counsel needs to clarify when she heard the ugly things about Milan Lukic. I don't think it was her testimony that she heard them all after he got on the bus. I think he's assuming something that is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Then Your Honours she can clarify on me. She had started to answer before Mr. --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... she did not know this individual. She did not know Milan Lukic until other people told her it was Milan Lukic. She testified she didn't know anything about him. So now, all of a sudden, she knows stuff about him. This is a very interesting development. I think I am a entitled to -- and I think I'm entitled to pursue it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, you can raise this issue in re-examination. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, madam, could you please complete your answer and tell me what is it that you learned and how long it took for these people who were telling you that -- introducing you to Milan Lukic, essentially at that time on the bus, how long it took them to tell you all these bad things about Milan Lukic that you now say you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Sir, I never said in any of my statements that I knew what he had done. I only said that I did not know him until that time. As for the stories, I had heard them before leaving Visegrad on the 14th of June. I heard those from other people, and I don't want to discuss that because I did not participate in any of his crimes. I did not observe them, and he never heard me, therefore I cannot testify to his acts.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you didn't answer my question. From whom and when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I can't tell you that and I don't want to talk about that. I don't want to talk about his deeds and I'd rather not answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You have testified here under oath that you did not know Milan Lukic before he stepped on the bus. You did not know of him. You also testified that you pulled your --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic, if you look at the record, you'll see the interpreters are complaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, just mindful of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, you have testified here under oath and under penalty of perjury, that you did not know of Milan Lukic before you stepped on the bus. You also testified under oath and under penalty of perjury, do you understand what those things mean, first of all, penalty of perjury?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's been said repeatedly to this witness, I would ask that the Court if such instructions need to be given to the witness that they be given by the Court. The witness has given an affirmation before she gave her evidence here and this constant badgering of does she realise she is under the penalties of perjury, I would ask that counsel be directed to refrain from such language of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, had Mr. Groome refrained from such language with our witnesses, I could see his point, but they used the most foulest of accusations against Defence witnesses in this case, Your Honour. The most foulest. And, therefore, I take umbrage that Mr. Groome repeatedly stepping up on these witnesses and saying that I'm badgering to them. I'm entitled to put my case to them, I'm entitled to cross-examine and confront them and confront them with the evidence, which I'm doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll determine whether you badger. Witness, what counsel is saying to you is that you have taken an oath to speak truthfully and that is what you should do and if you do not, then you commit an offence. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, you have testified to those things and now you have said that the reason you pulled and Mr. Kustura's pant leg was because you feared for his safety due to what you knew about Milan Lukic, what you heard about him; so it's quite critical to your testimony today that I know when and from whom you heard these bad things because you said it was before your departure so when and from whom did you hear these bad things about Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Before the convoy departed on the 14th, I heard a lot of things about him. I did not see any of those, it is one thing to hear something and another thing to see something. I don't want to talk about things I didn't see, only about what I heard. There are relevant witnesses who survived some of those things and they can tell you about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you hear enough bad things about Milan Lukic that would lead you to embellish your recollection so as to perhaps change a date or add facts as to how you knew it was Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I don't want to discuss those deeds of his. That's what I said. I don't want to discuss his evil deeds over other people. I did not participate in them and I did not see them. I don't want to discuss them. And it should be discussed with those who were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I also object to the insinuation that a date has been changed. Her statements have been consistent on that point since 1996, which was well before anyone could have known that that would be relevant in this case in which the defendant was arrested in 2005.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Of course the date was relevant in 1992 because that's when it was reported.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we've heard testimony in this courtroom of problems with convoys, convoys being cancelled in the same time-period that you are talking about. Convoys going across Sjemec the same road that you described being cancelled due to conflict and fighting in that region. Do you know anything about that? Your story doesn't seem to have that, I'd like to know why. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. My convoy was not stopped. We only stopped at a couple of locations so that people could go into the forest because they had to pee or similar things but that was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You said you do not know about my stories, they aren't my stories, ma'am. VG-141 in her sworn statement talks about a convoy that was cancelled - excuse me, can I finish - about a convoy that was cancelled going across the same road that your convoy took and it was cancelled due to fighting. Combat, active combat on that road. Do you deny that there was constantly combat on that road, the Sjemec road going towards Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure there is a foundation for this question. The witness has only testified to having been on that road on one particular day, I don't know what she can say about constant combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The VG-141 was talking about precisely the 15th and 16th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think she was speak being the 16th and 17th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you aware, Witness, of combat on that road, the Sjemec road going towards Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know anything about it. When my convoy was passing through, there was none of it. I can't speak for other convoys.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have just about five minutes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about something that you had to have seen if not the combat. We've had testimony and, indeed, documentation that three Serb soldiers, including Vlatko Trifkovic from Lijeska were killed. Their car burnt at the Tablja repeater on the road towards Sjemec, near Lijeska and that that car remained there for several days burnt out at that junction by the Tablja repeater. Did you see that burnt out car that other witnesses saw as late as the 15th of June on that road? Did you see that burnt out car on the 14th of June 1992 when your convoy passed the Tablja location by Lijeska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I did not. It is impossible to see everything. My children were there. I couldn't see everything and not all of the people on the bus could see the same thing. I did not see that. It wasn't a trip I was on. Our future was uncertain.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd like to ask now, when you arrived at the location that you arrived, you indicated that I believe you said Zeljko Tasic came on to the bus and issued some instructions. Now, in your proofing statement with Mr. Farr, there appear to be some confusion over several individuals by the name of Tasic who you refer to in your various statements. So I'd like to ask you, do you have difficulty distinguishing between Zarko, Veljko and Zeljko Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: No, that's not difficult for me because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is there a reason why you mistook them in one of your prior statements, ma'am, if you don't have difficulty differentiating between them? How could that error happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: They are similar names, first and last names, and during the typing they made a mistake because there's Zeljko Tasic and Veljko Tasic, so instead of saying Veljko Tasic and Zarko Tasic, instead of Zarko Tasic, the man exists he is an ordinary citizen, a worker like me; anyway, instead of Zarko Tasic, they Tasic, Zarko, his job, they said worked in the military department but it wasn't Tasic, Zeljko, Zarko but Veljko who worked there; so it was the same surname but not the same first name and they made a mistake in typing the names out because Zeljko Tasic was an active duty policeman in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to Zeljko Tasic, he was in your bus going towards the direction you were going, was he, when you set out from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: How do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, did he ride on the bus with you when you left Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: It was Goran Pecikoza who was on my bus --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... when you set out from Visegrad. I have very limited time, and I need you to answer the questions I pose.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: When we set out from Visegrad, I didn't see Zeljko Tasic in the bus, but in front of me, there was Goran Pecikoza, a colleague from work, but I didn't see Zeljko Tasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Goran Pecikoza?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: One moment. Ma'am, at the Bosnian court case against Mr. Zeljko Lelek there was testimony from Mr. Pecikoza indicating that he was actually in France during the time-period of this alleged incident. Does that refresh your recollection as to whether, in fact, Goran Pecikoza was on the bus with you as you set out from Visegrad as say on 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Goran Pecikoza was in my bus 100 percent. I'm absolutely certain. He was armed with an automatic rifle wearing a police uniform, the thick kind of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now I'd like to return again to Zeljko Tasic, because how do you account for Zeljko Tasic -- first of all, Zeljko Tasic is not from Isevic Brdo where you ended up, is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where your convoy ended up, I believe it was Isevic Brdo, Mr. Tasic is not located there, he doesn't come from there, does he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Who is not from where? From there?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Zeljko Tasic. He does not hail from those parts, does he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: He is not from those parts, but he came as an escort from the convoy from Visegrad. He came up there. I didn't see him during the journey anywhere until he entered our bus at Isevic Brdo and told us that the men from 15 to 65 should leave the bus -- or rather should stay in the bus where the women, children and people above that age should leave the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And you say that you did not see him at all during the convoy. You didn't see him when the buses stopped; is that correct? When persons got out to relieve themselves, you did not see him at that point escorting convoy, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Well, I saw him up there at Mangalin Han where we were boarding the buses, he was among the Serb soldiers there, and when we set off in the morning, but while we were on the square, I didn't see him there. As Isevic Brdo, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mean when people were relieving themselves, after they left Visegrad, is that where they saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you were boarding the buses. Was that where the busses had stopped to allow passengers to relieve themselves after you had left Visegrad, is that where you claim you saw Zeljko Tasic with other soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: How do you mean in other places?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, you just said that you saw him up there where we were boarding the buses among the Serb soldiers there. Where is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think she said Mangalin Han.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we stepped off after we had left the village of Dubovik to be transported from Mangalin Han to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Your last question, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's interesting to note, ma'am, that this reference to Mr. Tasic does not appear in your ICTY statement. Ma'am, I put it to you that due to what you had heard about Milan Lukic, all the bad things that he had done, the things you don't want to discuss here today, because of those bad things your testimony is painted against him and does not accurately reflect the dates of your travel and the persons you saw there; isn't that correct, ma'am? And that's why you don't want to talk about the bad things that Milan Lukic did and how you know about them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I'm not somebody who lies or invents things that I didn't see, and even if my father had done something, I would have said you did such and such, but rumours are rumours, and if your eyes see something that's something different, so I don't want to testify against that man based on stories told by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, very briefly, can you tell us who was Zarko Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Zarko Tasic was from a village called Tosici. He was a worker. I think he worked in the partisan [phoen] factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. Very briefly, who was Veljko Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Veljko Tasic was -- well, I don't know what post he had in the military department. It was called the military department at the time, but he was a neighbour of mine anyway and I knew him very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you. And briefly who was Zeljko Tasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Zeljko Tasic is younger than me and he was an active-duty policeman at the police station in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Which of those three men did you see at Isevic Brdo on the 14th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: At Isevic Brdo I saw Zeljko Tasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Which of those men did you see at Mangalin Han as you were boarding the buses on the 14th of June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: At Mangalin Han I also saw Zeljko Tasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer to bring up ERN X017-6218 through 6223, which is a B/C/S document, and the associated English translation which is the same ERN with the extension ET at the end. And put those on the split screens, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall giving a statement to the BiH Agency for Investigation and Documentation Gorazde department on 15 July, 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: I think --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer of whether you remember or not, the translator did not understand you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Whether I remember giving it, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in on the bottom of the first page of the B/C/S document?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please have the second page of the English version -- the middle of the second page of the English version and the bottom of the third page of the B/C/S version displayed on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, there's a section of this statement beginning the words -- with the words: "On 14 June, 1992, five or six aggressors soldiers..." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: In Bosnian, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, it's nine lines from the bottom in the Bosnian version. Can you please read aloud that sentence and the next three or four sentences through to the name "Zeljko Tasic"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: "On the 14th of June, 1992 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness speak up when she is reading, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, could you please speak into the microphone and speak a little louder. The portion beginning with [B/C/S spoken] in your language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: "In the village of Donja Dubovik where there were about 30 Bosniak civilians, five to six members of the aggressor soldiers turned up, Bosanska Jagodina, Veletovo, and Crnici, and there was Maric, Dusan. One of them was Dusan, Maric. They told us to leave immediately and that there were buses waiting for us up on the road. "When we went down to the road, I recognised among the aggressor soldiers, Ljupko Tasic, Mirko Tasic, Dusan Maric, Zjelko Tasic, the former active-duty policeman at the Visegrad SJB" --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, that's sufficient. Is that statement accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would tender this as a Prosecution exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be given Exhibit P330 admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we now please bring up ERN 0642-7095 through 7100. That's in Bosnian, and the English translation with the same ERN and the extension -ET.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall giving a statement to the Gorazde criminal police sector of the Ministry of Interior of the Federation of BiH in 2003 in connection with an investigation of Nenad Tanaskovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can you look at the signature in the middle of the page of the document in your language. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as your 2003 statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, do.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Could we please display the bottom portion of the fifth page of the English document, and the middle portion of the fifth page of the B/C/S document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll stipulate it contains the exact word for word as the last one as if they were just copied or retyped.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I've got one more reference in this document then. The top portion of the page 6 of the English version, and the bottom portion of the fifth page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Witness, do you see the sentence which begins with the word: "Milan Lukic came on board our bus at one moment looking for Esad Kustura"? In your language it starts with the words [B/C/S spoken].

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: "Milan Lukic came on board our bus at one moment looking for Esad Kustura, and several moments later on orders from Ljupko Tasic. Next to the bus I then noticed" --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Thank you, Witness. Is that statement accurate?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-136
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender this as a Prosecution exhibit under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P331 admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: May I confer for a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no more questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Farr. Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How many more witnesses for the day?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's one more witness, VG-22. I expect that he will be very, very brief. While we are talking about scheduling, Your Honour, the -- I think the Chamber is aware of the difficulties with VG-112. Hopefully they will -- that problem will be progressed sometime today and I think people are actively working on it. And then the only other two remaining witnesses for the Prosecution rebuttal case, Dr. Wil Fagel, he is unable to come until Wednesday, and VG-94 arrives here tomorrow, so I expect that we'll conclude all of our rebuttal evidence Wednesday morning, Your Honour, but unless something miraculous happens with VG-112, I don't expect that he will be here tomorrow, and there will be no witnesses for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll grant the protection, the voice protection sought by the next witness, and a new number.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Perhaps if we go into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit, and you may begin, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. VG-148, the Chamber has extended protective measures to you, including the use of a pseudonym, that pseudonym being VG-148, the distortion of your facial image, and distortion of your voice. I'd like to begin my questions to you by asking you to take a look at a pseudonym sheet to confirm your identity, your name, and your date of birth. The usher is now showing you a pseudonym sheet. I'd ask you to confirm. Is that your name and your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask that you please sign it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Before that's brought to up Their Honours to see, if the witness would take another look at it. There's a person there identified on the sheet as MLD 1. That person also has protective measures, so I would ask you that you never refer to that person by name. I will refer to that person as MLD 1 at all times, and I ask you to do the same. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, just I would tender that into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this document will shall given Exhibit P332, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask we go into private session for a few background questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, some very limited issues have arisen over the course of this trial, which you may have relevant evidence of. The first has to do with a car that Dragan Tomic drove in the spring and summer of 1992. Before I ask you my first question -- or let me ask you my first question. Did you know Dragan Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe your relationship with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, we grew up together. We went to high school together, and afterwards we were in rather close contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have information about the car he was driving in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, as to being general and vague. I think we need to specify specific months so that we're very clear as to what this witness is testifying about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I was attempting to avoid leading him. My attention is to focus in as soon as he responds.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the car he was driving in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead then, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what car he was driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Dragan Tomic drove a Peugeot 405.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What colour was that Peugeot 405?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: White.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know under what circumstances he acquired that car to drive?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe those circumstances for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Your Honours, that car was the property of the company we had mentioned earlier where I used to work, and on one occasion Dragan Tomic called me on the phone, asked me where the car was. I told him, and then he asked me if I could lend him that car because the police force was short of vehicles, and of course I said yes. After that telephone call, the car was made available to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, when did he ask you for this car? As best you're able, what was the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, you see, that was two days after the arrival of the Yugoslav People's Army at the hydro power-plant in Visegrad, which was the 17th of April, 1992, or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you yourself deliver the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe for us how you did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: It happened like this: At that time I was staying with my parents, and since it was very dangerous to move around, Dragan Tomic sent a car with two policemen who drove me to the location of the Peugeot. Of course, we first took the keys that had been kept by a certain man because I did not have the car myself. Then we drove to the police station. He sent his man to take the keys, and that's how I delivered the car to them. And afterwards, the policeman drove me back to the house where they had picked me up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said in your answer, "He sent his man to take the keys ..." Did you give the keys to a particular person, and if you did, do you know the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes. I personally gave the keys to him, and that gentleman's name was Vidoje Andric, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After giving the car keys to Vidoje Andric, how long did you remain in the Visegrad area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Around 30 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During that 30-day period, did you ever see this white Peugeot again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you able to see who was driving the car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes. Most of the time, I recognised the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is the name of the driver?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: The car was almost always driven by the same man to whom I had given the keys, Andric.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see it driven at other times by different people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During that 30-day period, did you ever see Vidoje Andric or Dragan Tomic drive a car other than the white Peugeot that belonged to your company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, you see, I think -- they also had a VW Golf - white, also - and I think they used that car, too, sometimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever see either man drive a red car?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to change topics. I'd like to speak to you about MLD 1. I'd again remind you that -- to take care to refer to this person by -- as MLD 1. You've described your relationship to and relationship with MLD 1 in private session. My question for you is: After the war, did you and MLD 1 ever share your experiences about what happened in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: It's frequently a subject of conversation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you assist us by characterising how often you would speak with him, and recognising it is an approximation, speak to him about your experiences in Visegrad during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Your Honours, the matter is discussed when the situation is favourable, when we are in the privacy of his house or our house -- my house or in a very close circle of friends, not otherwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did MLD 1 ever describe to you an event in which Milan Lukic saved his life?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did MLD 1 ever tell you that he went to Belgrade in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: He never mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Given the nature of your relationship with MLD 1, is it your view that if those two things happened it would be a matter that you likely both would have discussed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation as to what MLD might have thought of the relationship and what MLD might have wanted to share as part of that relationship.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just asking him to limit it to his view of the relationship, not necessarily MLD 1's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I will allow it as to whether it's the kind of issue that would have come up in conversations between you. He can speak to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: VG-148, can you please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question to you is given how you describe the relationship between yourself and MLD 1, is it your view that -- if he had gone to Belgrade in June of 1992, if Milan Lukic had saved his life during the course of the war, that that is something that he would have mentioned to you in your discussions about the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, you see, it would certainly be discussed because it would have been very interesting, but he never mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, did you and MLD 1 discuss your personal lives; for example, your relationships, girlfriends, loves?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: We did talk about that, too, because we were really close.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he ever tell you in the spring of 1992 that he was engaged to be married to a woman who lived in the Dusce area of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he ever move, to your knowledge, to the Dusce area of Visegrad to live with a woman?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: As far as I know, and I think I know these things well, he never lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was in a serious relationship during the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us where -- if you know, where that woman lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes, I know. Certainly I do, because we discussed this frequently. He had a serious relationship with a girlfriend who lived in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, VG-148. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: VG-148, as you have heard my name is Dan Ivetic, and it is now my task to pose some questions to you on behalf of Defence of Milan Lukic. Sir, to start off with I'm going to start backwards, I think, from the themes presented by the Prosecution. First of all, sir, did MLD 1 ever tell you that he was going to testify for the defence of Milan Lukic before appearing and testifying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And yet he did testify. You found that out from the Prosecution; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes. I found that out recently here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So despite your close relationship, he didn't feel he could safely reveal to you that he was a witness for the Milan Lukic defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really speculate as to the reasons why he hadn't told me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, he testified here as to his fear of how giving such testimony would be received by others in the Bosnian Muslim community. Did you know of that fear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I don't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, let me phrase it a different way. You will agree with me, will you not, that Milan Lukic is not a very popular person in the Bosnian Muslim community. Isn't that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And would you also agree with me that in the Bosnian press, including the TV and print, there's been a large outcrying of negative sentiments directed towards Milan Lukic, his attorneys, and defence witnesses led by, among others, Ms. Bakira Hasecic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, sir, to tell you the truth, I don't read too much. I haven't got the time, but everybody interprets what is written in their own way, so I don't have a particular opinion about these write-ups.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You don't read the Dnevni Avaz? You don't watch Federation Channel 1 TV? You don't watch TV Hajat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I read everything you have enumerated, and I watch everything you have enumerated, but not very thoroughly. I can't say that I follow it thoroughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: But you will not -- you will not dispute with me that the media has paid close attention to this trial and that the sentiment within the media in Bosnian is very much negative towards Mr. Milan Lukic, whatever the reason may be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, listen, there is coverage on the media, that's true, but I told you, when it comes, say, for example to Dnevni Avaz, I have a person that is tasked with going through that paper to see whether there's anything in it that would be of interest to me. And as for the rest, to tell you the truth, I just skip over that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: Have you had occasion to be in contact with other Bosnian Muslims such as yourself who hail from Visegrad, and what is their assessment of Milan Lukic? Is it positive or negative?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes. This is discussed, and the assessment is very negative mostly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And so if we were to return to MLD 1 for a second, would you agree with me that it would be very illogical and perhaps even unwise for MLD 1 to advertise the fact that Milan Lukic helped him, saved his life, and is a good person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, in order to answer that question, the best thing to say would be that it would be such a huge miracle that he would have told the closest persons around him that because that does not represent any danger whatsoever to him, nor is that any sort of demonisation or anything of the sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, wouldn't you agree me that MLD 1, you'd have to defer to him as to whether he felt afraid or not; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I apologise. I truly did not understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As for whether or not MLD 1 felt any fear, you would have to defer to him. He knows the ultimate answer to that. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, in fact, he didn't tell you that he was testifying even. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, according to my calculations, you would have left Visegrad sometime in the middle of May 1992. Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So I'm going to ask you, sir, did you have occasion in May and June of 1992 to regularly go to bars or cafes with MLD 1 so as to know with whom he socialised?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, all the way up until the 16th of May we would see each other almost every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: After May 16th, when was the next time that you saw MLD 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: When -- when I came to Zenica from Sarajevo, that was March or April of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So for approximately a full year, you were not in contact with MLD 1. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And again, I'd like to ask you: You'd have to defer to MLD 1 for his experiences during that year, in particular during June of 1992, because you weren't there and had no contact with him. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Your question was quite long, and I didn't get the initial part of it. What's the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, insofar as you were not present in Visegrad with MLD 1, specifically in June of 1992, you would have to defer to him as to his knowledge of the facts that he lived through during that time-period when you were not there, when you were not with him. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
