utterances.text: Well, yes. During that period of time, we were not together. Later on, we met up again and began socialising again.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd like to move to the first topic that was discussed. With respect to -- you said that Mr. -- that Mr. Tomic had sent his man, Vidoje Andric, to pick up the keys to the white Peugeot. At the time in question, that is to say that would have been in April of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What position did Dragan Tomic have at that point in time in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: At that time, he was a police commander. That's what the post was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I correct that Vidoje Andric was one of the other policeman that was engaged in the security detail for Commander Tomic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, see, here I'm not sure whether he was officially employed with the police, but based on contacts I know that he was more of his body-guard, personal body-guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. And there are other individuals in addition to Vidoje Andric who would accompany Commander Tomic and serve as his body-guards as you've coined that term?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Now, all those times that you saw Tomic and Andric driving around in the white Peugeot and other vehicles - you mentioned a white Golf, as well - that would all be in April and May of 1992, you have no knowledge of anything in Visegrad, personally with your own eyes, after May 16th, 1992, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Your Honours, I didn't quite understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Reformulate, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, you don't have any first-hand knowledge of what, how often, and where Vidoje Andric and Dragan Tomic drove around in June of 1992 or the second half of May 1992, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: During the period of time when I was absent from Visegrad, I don't know any details concerning that, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, we've had many witnesses here who have said that during that time-period when you weren't in Visegrad, Dragan Tomic was driven by Vidoje Andric and Milan Lukic and others in a red Passat. You can't dispute that fact, can you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I didn't hear about that, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, since you weren't there, would you have to defer to people who were there during at that time-period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, I didn't ask, but even if you didn't ask anyone this was a topic of the conversation. This was always an interesting topic for the residents of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So did you or did you not hear that Dragan Tomic and Vidoje Andric would be seen driving around a red vehicle, specifically a Passat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: See, here, I have never heard that they ever drove in that vehicle. That vehicle was always mentioned in relation to Milan Lukic in that context no matter whom I talked to, and I talked both to Bosniaks and Serbs after the war. This was always linked to the name of Milan Lukic, the red Passat.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is it your testimony here today that you've never heard of Vidoje Andric being linked to any such red automobile in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, one could say so. Vidoje Andric is not such an interesting individual, and I have no information concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask for Exhibit 1D126 that's already been admitted into evidence be shown to the witness on the e-court monitors.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, sir, when the photograph in question comes up, I'm going to ask you about the individual on the left with the vest on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can zoom in on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, looking at this photograph, the individual on the left with the vest on, that's the same Vidoje Andric that you gave the keys to, Tomic's man, Tomic's bodyguard, that would drive around with Commander Tomic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Yes, that's the person.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the individual sitting next to him with his arm around him, the same uniform, that's Milan Lukic, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, I can't say with hundred percent certainty. I didn't know this man before.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fair enough. Now, the car that these gentleman are sitting on, that's definitely not a white Peugeot, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm not going to ask you to opine as to what type of vehicle this red vehicle is, but I'm going to ask you this question: Having seen this photograph, do you now have reason to reconsider the possibility that Vidoje Andric and Dragan Tomic and Milan Lukic drove more than one car, including the red one that is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Forgive me, but you always put quite long questions. Vidoje Andric was of no particular interest, either to me or to others. Now, as to whether he drove in that particular vehicle, I really wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So you can neither confirm nor deny that Vidoje Andric, Milan Lukic, and Dragan Tomic may have driven around in a red vehicle, especially during those time-periods when you were not present in Visegrad. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: I have no personal knowledge of that. If you are interested, though, if you're quite interested in that, I can tell you what I have heard from friends, neighbours, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, sir, I'm only interested in your personal knowledge and -- and information that you have to assist us, and I believe that you've given it to us. Thank you, sir for your testimony. Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions on re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, neither Vidoje Andric or Dragan Tomic are alive today, are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: They're not alive. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know how they died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just in a sentence, could you tell us how it was that they died?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Based on what I know, they were killed when their vehicle hit a leftover mine on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know what vehicle they were driving?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was a white Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what's the date or approximate date of when they died in this white Golf?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS VG-148
utterances.text: Perhaps the end of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for giving it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a couple of administrative matters. The Chamber's witness Huso Kurspahic arrives tonight and will be in The Hague about 9.00 p.m. He can testify tomorrow, but VWS would prefer if his testimony doesn't begin first thing in the morning because his trip today has been long. VG-94, who is a Prosecution rebuttal witness, was initially scheduled by the Prosecution to testify tomorrow. According to the latest information from the Prosecution, VG-94 is now scheduled to testify on Wednesday. She arrives on Tuesday evening. No reason for this rescheduling has been given by the Prosecution. Now, we should be able to hear VG-94 on Wednesday provided we hear Huso Kurspahic tomorrow, and that would be the best use of the Court's time. Can we move now to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 7th day of April, 2009, at 9.50 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: [Private session] [Confidentiality lifted by order of Chamber]
--- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 3.11 p.m.,
